text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- National Electric Power Authority may soon embark on mass disconnections of consumers, whose total debts now amount to 12 billion naira.

- Various airlines owe Nigerian aviation authorities a total of 1.1 billion naira, for overfly and en route charges. Biggest debtor is Nigeria Airways, followed by Cameroon Airlines, Ethiopian Airlines and Air Afrique.
- National Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers complains about the alleged arrest of 33 union members at Port Harcourt, and says it may trigger crisis in the oil industry.
- Nigerian Ports Authority begins probe of alleged 1.0 billion naira fraud.
- Fear grips bank employees as restructuring programmes in 1997 may lead to extensive job losses.
- The Central Bank is considering a possible rescue plan for Crystal Bank, according to its managing director.

- Hints emerge of a heated pre-budget debate over foreign exchange policy, where Finance Minister Anthony Ani defended the current autonomous exchange rate of 80 naira to the dollar, while others pushed for a revaluation to 60 naira to the dollar.
- Government may have decided to phase out pre-shipment inspection for imports and exports from this year, and the one percent charges that go with the system.
- Domestic airlines continue to operate skeletal services following a shortage of Jet-A1 aviation fuel which began last week.
